content: 1. For respiratory tract and soft tissue infections, patients weighing 40 kg (88 lbs) or more should receive 250 to 500 mg of ampicillin every 6 hours. Patients weighing less than 40 kg (88 lbs) should be dosed at 25 to 50 mg/kg/day, divided into equal doses administered every 6 to 8 hours. 2. For infections of the gastrointestinal and genitourinary tracts, including those caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae in females, patients weighing 40 kg (88 lbs) or more should receive 500 mg every 6 hours. Patients weighing less than 40 kg (88 lbs) should be dosed at 50 mg/kg/day, divided into equal doses administered every 6 to 8 hours. 3. In the treatment of chronic urinary tract and intestinal infections, frequent bacteriological and clinical evaluations are necessary. Doses smaller than those recommended should not be used. Higher doses are advised for persistent or severe infections. In cases of stubborn infections, therapy may need to continue for several weeks, and clinical and/or bacteriological follow-up may be required for several months after therapy has ended. 4. For urethritis in males caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae, adults should receive two doses of 500 mg each, administered 8 to 12 hours apart. Treatment may be repeated or extended if necessary. For complications of gonorrheal urethritis, such as prostatitis or epididymitis, prolonged and intensive therapy is recommended. 5. In cases of gonorrhea with suspected primary syphilitic lesions, darkfield examinations should be performed before initiating treatment. For cases where concomitant syphilis is suspected, monthly serological tests should be conducted for at least four months. 6. The doses for the aforementioned infections can be administered via either intramuscular or intravenous routes. A switch to oral ampicillin may be made when appropriate. 7. For bacterial meningitis in adults and children, the recommended dosage is 150 to 200 mg/kg/day, divided into equal doses administered every 3 to 4 hours. Treatment may begin with intravenous drip therapy and continue with intramuscular injections. 8. For septicemia in adults and children, the recommended dosage is 150 to 200 mg/kg/day. Therapy should start with intravenous administration for at least three days, followed by intramuscular administration every 3 to 4 hours. 9. Treatment for all infections should continue for at least 48 to 72 hours beyond the point when the patient becomes asymptomatic or evidence of bacterial eradication is obtained. A minimum of 10 days of treatment is recommended for infections caused by Group A beta-hemolytic streptococci to prevent acute rheumatic fever or acute glomerulonephritis. 10. Only freshly prepared solutions of ampicillin should be used. Intramuscular and intravenous injections must be administered within one hour of preparation, as the potency of the drug may significantly decrease after this period. 11. For intramuscular use, dissolve the contents of the vial with the specified amount of Sterile Water for Injection, USP, or Bacteriostatic Water for Injection, USP. While the 1-gram and 2-gram vials of Ampicillin for Injection, USP, are primarily intended for intravenous use, they may be administered intramuscularly if the 250 mg or 500 mg vials are unavailable. Dissolve 8 mL of Sterile Water for Injection, USP, or Bacteriostatic Water for Injection, USP, to achieve a concentration of 250 mg/mL. 12. Ampicillin for Injection, USP, 125 mg, is primarily intended for pediatric use and serves as a convenient dosage form when small parenteral doses of the antibiotic are required. 13. For direct intravenous use, reconstitute the solution as directed above before diluting it with an intravenous solution. Stability studies indicate that ampicillin sodium retains more than 90% of its activity at specified temperatures and time periods. Only the solutions listed above should be used for intravenous infusion of Ampicillin for Injection, USP. 14. The concentration of the drug, as well as the rate and volume of infusion, should be adjusted to ensure that the total dose of ampicillin is administered before the drug loses its stability in the solution being used.
